quizzes.title: Checkpoint 1 — Strategy and Audience
quizzes.intro: Positioning, segments, journey, and channel intent.

questions.prompt: Digital marketing is best understood as:

options.text: A system for reaching audiences, communicating value, and guiding action with measurement

questions.explanation: Effective marketing connects audience, message, channels, and learning loops.

wrongExplanations.a: Randomness is not a strategy. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Tools follow strategy. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Research grounds relevance. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: A practical audience segment should include:

options.text: Who they are, desired outcome, obstacle, trust sources, and hesitations
A list of every human on Earth
No objections, because objections are negative

questions.explanation: Actionable segments capture jobs, barriers, and persuasion context.

wrongExplanations.a: Celebrity mentions are not segments. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Segments must be focused. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Objections are essential to address. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Matching content to journey stage means:

options.text: Giving awareness, consideration, and decision audiences different jobs to do
Using one identical post on every platform forever

questions.explanation: People at different readiness levels need different information and asks.

wrongExplanations.a: Premature hard sells waste cold attention. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Platforms and stages differ. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Measurement is required. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: For urgent emergency plumbing demand, prioritize first:
questions.explanation: Urgent intent aligns with search behavior close to the moment of need.

wrongExplanations.a: Podcasts are slow-burn brand, not emergency response. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Mood boards rarely capture emergency intent. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Missing the call-to-action wastes demand. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Specific about audience, situation, benefit, and reason to believe
Copied word-for-word from a competitor homepage

questions.explanation: Clear positioning guides messaging across channels. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: If it is for everyone, it is for no one.
wrongExplanations.c: Copying competitors erases differentiation. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Positioning should appear in customer-facing messaging. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

quizzes.title: Checkpoint 2 — Channels and Measurement
quizzes.intro: SEO, email, paid, analytics, and optimization.

questions.prompt: SEO at its core is about:

options.text: Aligning useful pages with real search intent and making them understandable

questions.explanation: Sustainable SEO serves intent with clear, crawlable, helpful pages.

wrongExplanations.a: Tricks decay and can harm trust. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Followers are not SEO. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Speed is part of modern SEO quality. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: You buy scraped lists without consent
Permission is real and messages are relevant to segments
You never measure clicks or conversions

questions.explanation: Consent plus relevance drive trust and performance. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Non-consensual lists damage deliverability and ethics. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Measurement guides improvement. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Fake urgency erodes trust. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: If ads get many clicks but few purchases, inspect first:

options.text: Only how to raise spend immediately
Landing page congruence, offer, trust, and checkout friction
Changing the company logo randomly each hour

questions.explanation: A strong CTR with weak conversion points to post-click experience or offer fit.

wrongExplanations.a: Spending more amplifies a broken funnel. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Analytics diagnose the issue. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Random logo thrash is not diagnosis. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Celebrating likes/reach that are disconnected from business goals

questions.explanation: Attention metrics matter only when tied to outcomes you care about.

wrongExplanations.a: Revenue impact is substantive. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Conversion is an outcome metric. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Retention quality matters. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Changing audience, offer, creative, and page all at once every hour
Forming a hypothesis and testing meaningful changes with enough signal
Stopping after one slow day forever

questions.explanation: Controlled learning beats chaotic tinkering. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Changing everything destroys attribution of cause. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: One day is rarely enough evidence. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Qualitative insight explains the “why.”. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz — Marketing Judgment
quizzes.intro: Integrate strategy, channels, ethics, and learning loops.

questions.prompt: Before launching ads, the most valuable artifact is often:

options.text: Clear positioning, audience definition, offer, and measurement plan
A promise to never read results

questions.explanation: Strategy artifacts prevent expensive confusion. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Creative without strategy underperforms. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Results reading is the point. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Untracked codes blind learning. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Acquiring users into a leaky experience wastes growth spend

questions.explanation: Retention and activation determine whether acquisition creates value.

wrongExplanations.a: Buckets leak without retention. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Email is legal with consent. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Content can support retention. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Dark patterns, fake scarcity, and hidden subscriptions

questions.explanation: Manipulative patterns create legal and brand risk. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Honesty is ethical. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Easy opt-outs respect people. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Permissioned proof is legitimate. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Attribution models should be treated as:

options.text: Useful approximations that need multiple lenses and experiments when stakes are high
A reason to ignore landing pages

questions.explanation: Attribution helps, but it is approximate; triangulate for big decisions.

wrongExplanations.a: No model is perfect truth. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Pages still matter. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Interviews still matter. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Empathy for customers and evidence from measurement
Tool purchases instead of messaging clarity

questions.explanation: Empathy creates relevance; evidence improves outcomes. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Untested gut is fragile. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Clarity beats tool sprawl. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Channels have different contexts. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
